author: Codex documentation author

scenarios.expected: Lead-time changes and audit facts are observable at the documented scope. The audit log is unavailable to other roles; timezone/channel limits and missing events are investigated rather than assumed.
scenarios.actual: Both rail entries read "Notifications"; the Organization one at /settings/reminders is headed "Reminder lead times" and the Personal one holds only that person's switches. Added 0, 4 and 11 to the organization list; a duplicate was refused with "4 days before is already on the list." and 731 with "Enter a whole number of days between 0 and 730."; zero rendered as "On the day"; Remove and a keyboard reorder both saved and survived a reload; reduced to one entry the row lost its Remove control, showed the only-lead-time lock, and an empty list was refused by the API. Delivery used a brand-new fictional Legal Team Member with no earlier briefing history, a saved Asia/Dubai timezone and their own preferences. The real queued notification.morning-round completed in the owned worker on the real clock; Mailpit delivered an actual briefing naming the 4-day and On-the-day Key dates and omitting the 11-day one, and the bell linked to the record's Key dates page rather than naming the Key date. Audit log: reached under Security, the Person, Action and Record filters combined and narrowed in turn, the From and To bounds became the browser's local calendar day in Asia/Dubai, an out-of-range window reported "No entry matches these filters.", Clear filters recovered, Search matched recorded audit text but not a Request answer's prose, Export CSV downloaded every matching entry, and Show older paged back. Legal and Contributor were redirected from the pane and refused 403 on GET /audit-log.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough, not a human user study; the author and the reviewer are different agents.
Verified on the owned lab at immutable source 6a8873db; final candidate compatibility belongs to DOC-025.
